Definition: from G5384 and στοργή (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian:--kindly affectioned.
BiblicalUsage: Philostorgos means tenderly loving, cherishing one's kindred, and it appears once, in Paul's picture of the church as a family. Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love, in honour preferring one another.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe tender affection is the church's family feeling: not cold duty but the warmth of kindred, preferring the other in honour.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
